alignments.note: Substantival numeral completed by the supplied generic *stripes*; the head stays on the numeral, which carries the lexeme (rule 31).
Verb with its subject pronoun and modal (rule 17), headed on the lexical verb (rule 24).
Object suffix → *him* (rule 18).
לֹא → *not*.
Verb with subject pronoun and auxiliary, discontinuous around the negative (rules 17, 25).
פֶּן → *lest*.
The second subordinator *if* answers to no morpheme: פֶּן already holds the *lest* written for it, and a conjunction holding an English word of its own is not a home for a second (rules 51, 55).
Verb with subject pronoun and modal, headed on the lexical verb.
The ASV recasts the לְ + infinitive as a coordinated finite clause and writes no preposition or complementizer for the לְ (rules 40, 52).
No conjunction morpheme stands in this clause, so the coordinating *and* the ASV supplies is its own unit and is not folded into the preposition or the verb beside it (rule 14, closing sentences).
Infinitive → *beat*.
Object suffix → *him* (rule 18).
עַל → *above*.
אֵלֶּה → *these*.

Adverbial accusative מַכָּה רַבָּה: the supplied *with* belongs to the noun whose case-function licenses it and which opens the Hebrew phrase (rule 33), the unit discontinuous around the adjective (rule 25). Attaching *with* to רַבָּה, the word it stands before in the English, was the competing reading.
רַב → *many*.
Apodosis waw takes the *then* written for it (rule 14).
Verb rendered *should seem vile*; the head is the complement carrying the lexeme (rule 44).
אָח → *brother*.
Suffix → *thy* (rule 18).

לְ before the construct noun עֵינֵי is rendered by the single English preposition *unto*, so rule 30's one-rendering condition is met and the two share one unit headed on the construct noun (rules 30, 23); the suffix keeps the *thee* written for it, exactly as בְּעֵינֶיךָ → *thee* does under rule 40's closing paragraph. Marking עַיִן `unrepresented` beside a preposition holding the whole word is what rules 30 and 22 forbid.
Suffix → *thee* (rule 18).

review_notes: Corrected: לְעֵינֶיךָ was split as *unto* on the preposition with עַיִן `unrepresented`. One English word is written for the preposition and its construct noun, so rule 30's compound-preposition sentence fuses them, headed on עַיִן (rule 23); the suffix keeps *thee*. Contrast DEU.25.9, where the ASV writes *in* and *the presence* and the split stands.
Two supplied words remain `added`: the *if* of *lest if*, which פֶּן cannot hold a second time (rules 51, 55), and the *and* of *and beat him*, for which no conjunction morpheme stands (rule 14).
The supplied *with* of *with many stripes* stays on מַכָּה under rule 33; giving it to רַבָּה was the materially competing reading.
